notes: W21 (2026-09-07): the router prices the fine DEM's pass height per land edge (W21a) and prunes dominated land modes exactly (W21b); the pass table is carried as f32, so the shipped-grid copy is 26 MB and the JS-side double copy is gone. Query and distance-map rows re-baselined DOWNWARD by the ratio measured on this runner, never by its raw numbers (this runner builds the target substrate in ~41-43 s against the 52 s baseline, so it is ~20% faster than the review runner): target query 1721 -> 1026 ms and distance map 1841 -> 1084 ms across the pruning in one bench each, 1671 -> 1149 and 1695 -> 1175 in a same-process probe; the conservative same-process ratio (0.69) carries 2600 -> 1800 and 2700 -> 1900. Dev query 37.5 -> 25.0 and distance map 24.9 -> 18.3 carry 60 -> 45 and 32 -> 24. Dev routingInitialize is raised 20 -> 40 on measured identity, not on W21: the row is one first call and is dominated by reading and instantiating the wasm module, which this runner measures at 35-50 ms for the pre-W21 module and the W21 module alike (two bench --check runs read 29 and 38 ms; the constructor itself is 3-5 ms at dev for either); the pruning scan adds nothing to it. Target routingInitialize and customize are left at 2500 / 2300: the same probe measures the first target construction at 1.2-2.0 s for the pre-W21 and W21 modules alike, and one bench under contention read 4.7 s / 2.2 s while three isolated engines in a row read 1.0-2.9 s / 0.8-1.7 s, so those two rows are runner noise today and not re-anchored on it. The dominance scan is inside customize and costs one pass over the cells per land-mode pair. W12 s2 (2026-09-05): solveStepMilliseconds is replaced by solveYearMilliseconds — milliseconds per YEAR of solve, which survives a change of schedule. The solve passes now take their own strides, so a step is no longer one 84-month firing at both grids: at dev the schedule is still uniform (every pass 84, clock 84, one step = 7 years, byte-identical) and at the shipped grid movement fires at 24 months against the reaction passes' 84, so the clock is their gcd of 12 and a step is one year. Baselines are the old per-firing baselines carried across by the ratio MEASURED ON THIS RUNNER, not reset to it (the runner is ~2.5x faster than the one that set 11/440): dev 11/7 = 1.6 unchanged, since dev's schedule is unchanged and it measured 0.55 vs 0.57 ms/yr under the old and new code; target 440/7 x 2.99 = 190, the measured 34.9 -> 104.8 ms/yr step up from the corrected hop share (W12 s1), which needs 3.5x the movement firings to carry the same span inside PEOPLE_MIGRATION_MAX_SHARE. Per-pass strides are what keep that multiplier off the other five passes: against one stride at migration's own bound the same 70 years cost 124.3 ms/yr on a cold world and 401.8 vs 243.6 ms/yr with every hearth primed (1.19x and 1.65x). The ratchet itself reads 0.74 dev / 112.42 target here against caps 1.92 / 228; that headroom is the carried review-runner baselines, not slack to spend. W6 (2026-09-03): tickMilliseconds is now the mean month over one 84-month movement cycle of the awake regime (growth yearly, movement every 84 months, most months empty), measured 0.8 ms dev / 16.4 ms target — re-baselined DOWNWARD from 12 / 220 (the monthly movement pass is gone by physics: foragers see forager room and hop at a grounded 23 km²/yr, each group's stride derives from its own bound). solveStepMilliseconds measured 8.2 / 416–426 on a review runner that was about a third slower than in the morning (the target substrate build took 52.5 s against 39 s for the same code); the two-flow pass prices two rooms per pair, about a fifth more than the mixed flow at the opening when every pair is priced; baselines 11 / 440 carry that and the runner drift. W5 (2026-09-03): solveStepMilliseconds is one solve-regime firing (84 months at both grids), ten serial firings from the opening, measured 5.6 ms dev / 233 ms target on the review runner (with hearths active a target firing is ~294 ms: the annual passes fire every firing); baselines 8 / 300 carry the same headroom as the tick rows. The awake tick measured 2.2 / 163 ms here (the migration pass now recomputes its row shares every firing and the arrival recorder runs per commit, +4 ms at target); tick baselines unchanged. W3 review re-anchor (2026-09-02) of the ROUTING rows only, upward: the router is untouched by W2/W3 but today's review container measures the target customize/query/distance-map phases ~20% above the W2 numbers (2183/2515/2626 ms vs 1800/2100/2200) and dev query fluctuates 43-72 ms; runner drift, not a regression, so the caps follow the measurement. People-tick rows unchanged: target 206 ms/tick serial cold here (W2: 169 cold / 210 pre-W2), dev 1.6 ms. Cursor's runner measured 2.6 / 122 ms; cross-runner numbers are not comparable, so baselines always come from the review runner. Values carry headroom; CI fails above 120%. Threads are real since W3 (shared-memory dispatch, 1 ms barrier slices); the cadence table in the bench output carries the per-config numbers and the <=30-minute Phase-1 ceiling remains open (W4).
